old_note: *In Jerusalem indeed I saw Him being crucified on a tree.* Ascension of Isaiah 11:20 names the wisdom-stream's direct external-witness historical-attestation of the crucified-on-a-tree-in-Jerusalem substance — the prophet-Yeshayahu (Isaiah)-saw-in-vision what the King walked at the historical-pivot. The framework reads the verse against Matt 27:35's *and they crucified him* — the wisdom-stream had named the operative-substance at the prophet-Yeshayahu-register; the historical-pivot at the cross is the seeing-what-Yeshayahu-saw substance walking-out. The framework reads this in continuity with John 12:41's *these things said Esaias (Isaiah), when he saw his glory, and spake of him* — the prophet Yeshayahu (Isaiah) saw the King at multiple registers (the holy-holy-holy-vision of Yeshayahu 6, the Suffering-Servant of Yeshayahu 53, the Ascension-of-Isaiah-11-vision of the King's-Bethlehem-birth-and-cross). The cross walks-out the substance the prophet saw-in-vision centuries before.
new_note: *And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.* (Matthew 27:35). *In Jerusalem indeed I saw Him being crucified on a tree:* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:20). Matthew tells of the crucifixion in a few plain lines and says it came to pass according to what was spoken by the prophet. The Ascension of Isaiah has Isaiah himself seeing it first, and naming the place: in Jerusalem, on a tree. What Matthew sets down as history, the prophet was shown beforehand.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:20 — *In Jerusalem indeed I saw Him being crucified on a tree.* Isaiah is shown the crucifixion ahead of time, in Jerusalem, on a tree.

old_note: *And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* Ascension of Isaiah 11:19 names the wisdom-stream's direct external-witness articulation of the descended-to-the-angel-of-Sheol substance — the King's-burial-and-descent-into-the-place-of-the-dead architecture. The framework reads the verse against Matt 27:60's *and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed* — the burial in Yoseph (Joseph) of Arimathea's rich-man's-tomb walks-out the Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 53:9's *he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death* substance AND is the historical-pivot of the descent-to-the-angel-of-Sheol architecture AI 11:19 names. The framework reads the substance carefully against Red Line #9 — the *roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him* substance reads in continuity with the framework's system-not-people posture per the four-costumes-and-their-victims architecture: the adversary-roused-the-leadership-of-the-second-Temple-aristocracy at the historical-pivot, NOT the substantial-Yahudah (Jewish)-people-as-a-whole; the framework rejects the inherited-Christian-replacement-theology weaponization of this verse against the Yahudim (Jews) as a people. The cross + the descent + the resurrection-on-the-third-day are the architecture the wisdom-stream named at the prophet-Yeshayahu-vision-register.
new_note: *And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed.* (Matthew 27:60). *And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:19). Matthew closes the day with the body laid in a new tomb cut in the rock and a great stone rolled to the door. The Ascension of Isaiah tells where the Beloved was while the body lay there: after they crucified Him, He descended to the angel of Sheol. The same verse says the adversary envied him and stirred up the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against him, not knowing who He was. The charge lies with the adversary who envied and stirred, and a people who did not know who they were handing over are the lost sheep, not enemies.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:19 — *they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* While the body lay in the sealed tomb, the Beloved went down to the angel of Sheol.
drafter_flag: Old note's reading of the Isaiah 53:9 tomb (rich man's grave) and its Red Line reference dropped from the text; kept its point that the verse is not a charge against the Yahudim (Jews) as a people.

old_note: *And likewise after the third day rise again and remain days.* Ascension of Isaiah 11:21 names THE direct external-witness verbal-anchor for the King's-third-day-Resurrection substance — the wisdom-stream-prophetic-substance Yeshayahu (Isaiah) walks-out in vision at the heavenly-substance-register the gospel-substance walks-out at the historical-pivot. The framework reads the verse against Matt 28:6's *He is not here: for he is risen, as he said.* The heavenly-messenger's-announcement at the empty-tomb is the operative-fulfillment of the substance AI 11:21 had named at the wisdom-stream-vision-register centuries before — the third-day-rise-again-substance the prophet-Yeshayahu (Isaiah) had seen-in-vision walks the same architecture Hosea 6:2's *after two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up* names at the Tanakh-register and Jonah 1:17's three-days-and-three-nights names at the pre-figuration-register. Per Yoshi's S32 sourcing-note (api/seed.py:EDITION_PROFILES["ascension-isaiah"]), AI is the *first witness* aligning with the framework's reading at the deepest external-witness level — pre-Nicene, late-1st / early-2nd CE, before the Constantine-era doctrinal-construct hardened. The remain-days-substance ties to the forty-days-between-Resurrection-and-Ascension per Acts 1:3. FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.
new_note: *He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6). *And likewise after the third day rise again and remain days.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:21). At the empty tomb the angel says that he is not here, for he is risen, as he said. The Ascension of Isaiah has Isaiah told the same in vision, that He will rise after the third day and remain days. The rising was not an afterthought, it was said before by Yahusha (Jesus) himself and seen before by the prophet, and the days he remained with his own after rising are the days the vision speaks of.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:21 — *after the third day rise again and remain days.* Isaiah is shown the rising after the third day and the days He remained, which the angel at the tomb announces as fulfilled.
drafter_flag: Old note named the forty days of Acts 1:3; I kept only a general sentence about the days He remained, since the live verse says only 'remain days'.

old_note: *And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* Ascension of Isaiah 11:19 names THE direct external-witness articulation of the adversary-roused-the-children-of-Yashar'el (Israel)-not-knowing-who-He-was substance — the system-not-people-architecture per Red Line #9 named at the wisdom-stream-vision-register. The framework reads the verse against Matt 28:11's Roman-watch reporting to the chief-priests and the bribery-cover-up that follows at vv.12-15. The substantial *they delivered Him to the king* substance names the corrupt-Sanhedrin-leadership-system-substance the apostle-Mattithyahu (Matthew) walks at-Matthew 26-27 — the leadership-system-substance corrupting-the-substance-of-the-people; the *not knowing who He was* substance names the people-as-victims-of-the-leadership's-deception-substance, NOT the categorical-anti-Yahudi (Jewish)-substance the inherited-Christian-collapse misuses. AI 11:19 names the architecture explicitly: the adversary (Sammael Satan per AI 11:41) is the substantial-source; the children-of-Yashar'el (Israel) are roused-against-Him not-knowing-who-He-was — the people-as-victims of-the-substantial-deception-the-leadership-handed-them. The chief-priests' bribery-cover-up at Matt 28:12-15 is the operative-form of the same architecture: the corrupt-leadership-system fabricating the anti-Resurrection-narrative and walking-it-out-into the broader-Yahudim (Jews)-community-substance. The substantial-system-not-people posture holds non-negotiable.
new_note: *Now when they were going, behold, some of the watch came into the city, and shewed unto the chief priests all the things that were done.* (Matthew 28:11). *And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:19). Matthew tells that some of the watch came into the city and showed the chief priests all that had been done, and the verses that follow tell of money given to the soldiers to carry a false story. The Ascension of Isaiah gives the order of it: the adversary envied him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against him, not knowing who He was. The line runs from the adversary through those who held the seat of leadership, and the many who were roused did not know, and are deceived sheep. It is a system that lied, and no verse here makes a whole people the enemy.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:19 — *the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was.* The adversary roused the people not knowing who He was, and Matthew shows the leadership answering the truth with a cover story.
drafter_flag: Same extra verse as card 4889 (11:19); this card carries the system-not-people point, 4889 the burial and descent. Old note's internal references removed.

old_note: *And the angel who conducted me said: "Understand, Isaiah": and I saw when He sent out the Twelve Apostles and ascended.* Ascension of Isaiah 11:22 names THE direct external-witness verbal-anchor for the Great Commission substance — the King-sending-out-the-Twelve-Apostles + the Ascension named in the same breath at the wisdom-stream-vision-register. The framework reads the verse against Matt 28:19's *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations* — the substantial-Great-Commission walks-OUT-FROM-Galilee-of-the-scattered-seed (per Matt 4:14-16 / Isaiah 9:1-2) INTO-the-territories-of-the-substantial-nations-substance the scattered-seed-of-both-houses is-substantively-among. AI 11:22 names the architecture explicitly: the King-substance sends-out-the-Twelve-Apostles + ascends — the same substance Matt 28:19-20 articulates at the gospel-pivot + Acts 1:8-11 articulates at the apostolic-pivot. The substantial-Twelve-Apostles substance walks the substantial-twelve-tribes-restoration-architecture-substance per Matt 19:28 (*ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)*) + Revelation 21:14 (the twelve-foundations-of-the-new-Yerushalayim (Jerusalem)) — the wisdom-stream had named the architecture; the gospel-substance names the operative-form. FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.
new_note: *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). *And the angel who conducted me said: "Understand, Isaiah": and I saw when He sent out the Twelve Apostles and ascended.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:22). Isaiah sees Him send out the Twelve Apostles and then ascend, and Matthew has the sending in his own words: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations. Twelve are sent because the twelve tribes are the ones being sought, and the nations are where the scattered of those tribes now live. We do not know the sheep by sight, so the word goes out broadly, and the sheep hear his voice.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:22 — *I saw when He sent out the Twelve Apostles and ascended.* The sending of the Twelve and the ascension are seen together, as Matthew's last words to the Twelve are spoken.
drafter_flag: Old note's Great Commission reading (the Twelve match the twelve tribes; the scattered among the nations) kept in plain prose; Matthew 19:28 and Revelation 21:14, which it cited, are not quoted here.

old_note: *And I saw how He ascended into the seventh heaven, and all the righteous and all the angels praised Him. And then I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory I told you that I could not behold.* Ascension of Isaiah 11:32 names THE direct external-witness verbal-anchor for the King's-Ascension-to-the-right-hand-of-the-Great-Glory substance — the operative-substance of Psalm 110:1's *Yahuah (the LORD) said unto my Adon (Lord), Sit thou at my right hand* the prophet-David walked at the Tanakh-register. The framework reads the verse against Matt 28:18's *All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* The substantial-Great-Glory at AI 11:32 is the Father — the Formless-Source per the framework's nature-of-God reading per Red Line #10; the substantial-right-hand-of-the-Great-Glory is the place from-which the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-the-Daniel-7:13-14 dominion-and-glory-and-a-kingdom-substance. The substantial-substance is the Father-Son-relational-architecture-substance — NOT-categorical-three-co-equal-persons-Trinitarian-substance the inherited-Christian-Nicene-Constantinople-collapse walks. The King's *all power is given unto me* names the Father-giving-the-Son the everlasting-dominion the prophet-Daniel walked at Daniel 7:14; AI 11:32 names the heavenly-vision-substance the gospel-substance enacts at the historical-pivot. The framework reads this in continuity with Philippians 2:9-11 (*Elohim (God) also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name*). FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.
new_note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18). *And I saw how He ascended into the seventh heaven, and all the righteous and all the angels praised Him. And then I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory I told you that I could not behold.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:32). The Ascension of Isaiah says He sat down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory the prophet could not behold. The Great Glory is the Father, the formless one, and the Son who took form sits at his right hand. When Yahusha (Jesus) says in Matthew that all power is given unto him in heaven and in earth, the word given tells the same story: the Son receives the power from the Father who gives it, and takes his seat beside him.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:32 — *I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory.* The Son sits at the right hand of the Great Glory, the Father, and Matthew has him say that all power is given unto him.
drafter_flag: Kept the Father/Son point: the Great Glory is the Father (formless), the Son receives the power as given. No doctrine asserted beyond that.

old_note: *And He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven. And I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.* Testament of Benjamin Ch 7:5 (TestXII ch 94:5 in the Charles concatenation, corresponding to traditional Test. Benjamin 9:3-5) names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the King's-ascending-from-Hades + passing-from-earth-into-heaven + the-lowly-upon-earth-and-glorious-in-heaven substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 28:18's *All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* The substantial-substance the wisdom-stream names at the kenosis-and-glorification architecture — the lowly-upon-earth (the form-of-the-servant the apostle-Sha'ul (Paul) names at Philippians 2:6-8) and the glorious-in-heaven (the substantial-right-hand-of-the-Great-Glory the AI 11:32 substance walks) — is the substantial-substance the King walks-out from-the-incarnation-at-Matt 1:23 to-the-substantial-Resurrection-and-Ascension-and-all-power-given-substance at-Matt 28:18. The substantial-Tanakh-substance walks the substantial Psalm 16:10 substance (*neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption*) + Psalm 68:18 substance (*Thou hast ascended on high*) + Ephesians 4:8-10 substance. (NOTE: Test. Benjamin 7:5 was previously cited at-S155-Matt-20:28 for the lowly-came-to-give-his-life-a-ransom-for-many substance; Matt 28:18 carries-forward the SAME verbal-anchor to the glorious-in-heaven half of the architecture — the kenosis-and-glorification substance bookended.)
new_note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18). *And He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven. And I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 139:5). Benjamin says the one who comes will ascend from Hades and pass from earth into heaven, lowly on the earth and glorious in heaven. After the cross and the tomb, Yahusha (Jesus) comes to His disciples and says all power is given to Him in heaven and in earth. The word Benjamin gave his sons is the road that ends in that sentence.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 139:5 — *He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven.* Benjamin foresees the ascent from Hades into heaven, and Yahusha (Jesus) states the power given Him in heaven and in earth.
drafter_flag: Stale old citations ('Ch 7:5', 'TestXII ch 94:5') replaced with live 139:5. This verse is also on the Matthew 20:28 card; the two cards use different halves of the verse. Old note's Psalm and Ephesians references and its internal cross-card note were dropped.

old_note: *And shall reveal His salvation to all Gentiles.* Testament of Benjamin Ch 8:6 (TestXII ch 95:6 in the Charles concatenation, corresponding to traditional Test. Benjamin 10:5) names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the salvation-revealed-to-all-Gentiles substance — the substantial-going-out-of-the-proclamation-substance the substantial-Great-Commission walks-out. The framework reads the verse against Matt 28:19's *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations.* The substantial-substance is the substantial-revelation-of-the-Father's-salvation-substance the Resurrected-King-substance walks-out through-the-substantial-Twelve-Apostles-substance into-the-substantial-territories-of-the-substantial-nations-where-the-substantial-scattered-seed-of-both-houses-is-substantively-among. The substantial-substance is NOT-the-substantial-categorical-grafting-of-the-substantial-nations-substance into-the-covenant; the substantial-substance is the substantial-revelation-of-the-Father's-salvation-going-BROADLY because the substantial-citizens-of-the-kingdom-substance are-substantively-scattered-among-the-territories-of-the-substantial-nations-substance and-the-substantial-substance-of-the-substantial-Father-knows-his-sheep-by-substance (John 10:27) NOT-by-our-sighting. The substantial-substance the wisdom-stream names walks-the-substantial-Great-Commission's scope-of-proclamation-substance.
new_note: *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). *For all these things they gave us for an inheritance, saying: Keep the commandments of Elohim (God), until Yahuah (Lord) shall reveal His salvation to all Gentiles.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:5). The fathers left their sons the commandments of Elohim (God) as their inheritance, to be kept until Yahuah (the Lord) reveals His salvation to all the Gentiles. When Yahusha (Jesus) says to go and teach all nations, the message goes out broadly because those it is for are scattered among them and are not known by sight. Benjamin's word has the order right: the commandments stay in the hands of the sons, and the salvation goes out to be heard.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:5 — *Keep the commandments of Elohim (God), until Yahuah (Lord) shall reveal His salvation to all Gentiles.* Benjamin's sons are left the commandments until the salvation is revealed to all the Gentiles, and Yahusha (Jesus) sends His own out to every nation.
drafter_flag: Stale old citations ('Ch 8:6', 'TestXII ch 95:6') replaced with live 140:5. Old note quoted only 'And shall reveal His salvation to all Gentiles'; I quote the whole live verse, which also carries the commandments, so Torah stands in the note.

old_note: *Then shall we also rise, each one over our tribe, worshipping the King of heaven, who appeared upon earth in the form of a man in humility. And as many as believe on Him on the earth shall rejoice with Him.* Testament of Benjamin Ch 8:7 (TestXII ch 95:7 in the Charles concatenation, corresponding to traditional Test. Benjamin 10:7-8) names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the substantial-twelve-tribes-rising-each-one-over-his-tribe-substance + worshipping-the-King-of-heaven-substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 28:10's *go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.* The substantial *my brethren* substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-at-v.10 is the substantial-gathered-remnant-of-the-substantial-twelve-tribes-of-Yashar'el (Israel)-substance per Psalm 22:22 (*I will declare thy name unto my brethren*) + Hebrews 2:11-12 + Matt 12:46-50 + Matt 25:40 — the substantial-substance the S87 Matt 25 thread `my-brethren-substance-distinguishing-the-seed-of-promise-from-the-categorical-nations` walks-out. The substantial-substance the wisdom-stream walks at TestXII 95:7 is the substantial-rising-of-the-twelve-tribes-each-one-over-his-tribe — the substantial-twelve-thrones-substance the King walks-at-Matt 19:28 (*ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)*) + Revelation 7:4-8 (the substantial-twelve-thousand-of-each-of-the-twelve-tribes-substance). The substantial-substance is the substantial-twelve-tribes-restoration-architecture-substance per Red Line #11.
new_note: *Then said Yahusha (Jesus) unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.* (Matthew 28:10). *Then shall we also rise, each one over our tribe, worshipping the King of heaven, [who appeared upon earth in the form of a man in humility. And as many as believe on Him on the earth shall rejoice with Him].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:7). After His resurrection Yahusha (Jesus) tells the women to carry word to His brethren, and the brethren He means are sons of Yashar'el (Israel). Benjamin pictures that same people rising from the dead, each patriarch over his own tribe, worshipping the King of heaven who appeared on earth in the form of a man. The Testament keeps the tribes by name and by order, and the Messiah (Christ) still calls them brethren.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:7 — *Then shall we also rise, each one over our tribe, worshipping the King of heaven.* Benjamin sees the patriarchs rising each over his tribe to worship the King, and Yahusha (Jesus) after rising calls His own brethren.
drafter_flag: Stale old citations ('Ch 8:7', 'TestXII ch 95:7') replaced with live 140:7. Old note's cross-references (Psalm 22, Hebrews 2, Matthew 12 and 25, Revelation 7, Matthew 19:28) and its thread slug are not on the card and were dropped.

old_note: *Then also all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame. And Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness; for when He appeared as Elohim (God) in the flesh to deliver them they believed Him not. And then shall He judge all the Gentiles.* Testament of Benjamin Ch 8:8 (TestXII ch 95:8 in the Charles concatenation, corresponding to traditional Test. Benjamin 10:8-9) names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the substantial-all-men-shall-rise-some-unto-glory-and-some-unto-shame substance — the substantial-Daniel-12:2-substance (*many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt*) carried-forward at-the-wisdom-stream-register. The framework reads the verse against Matt 28:18's *All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* The substantial-all-power-substance the King receives at v.18 is the operative-substance for the substantial-judging-substance the wisdom-stream names at TestXII 95:8 — the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-the-substantial-judgment-substance per Acts 17:31 (*because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained*) + the substantial Matt 25:31-46 sheep-and-goats-substance. The substantial *Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness* substance walks the substantial-substance the apostle-Kefa (Peter) walks at 1 Peter 4:17 (*judgment must begin at the house of Elohim (God)*) — the substantial-judgment-of-the-substantial-house-of-Yashar'el (Israel)-first walks the substantial-substance-of-the-substantial-Father's-substance-of-the-substantial-substance-walked.
new_note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18). *Then also all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame. And Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness; [for when He appeared as Elohim (God) in the flesh to deliver them they believed Him not].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:8). Benjamin says all men shall rise, some to glory and some to shame, and that Yahuah (the Lord) will judge Yashar'el (Israel) first because they did not believe Him when He appeared as Elohim (God) in the flesh. Yahusha (Jesus) says all power is given to Him in heaven and in earth, and a judge needs that power. Judgment beginning with the house of the fathers is the order the Testament lays out, and Yahusha (Jesus) is the one who holds the authority to carry it through.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:8 — *Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness.* Benjamin says Yahuah (the Lord) will judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, and Yahusha (Jesus) holds the power in heaven and in earth to do it.
drafter_flag: Stale old citations ('Ch 8:8', 'TestXII ch 95:8') replaced with live 140:8. Old note ran into the next verse (140:9, the Gentiles' judgment) and added Daniel 12:2, Acts 17:31, Matthew 25 and 1 Peter 4:17; none are on the card and they were dropped.

old_note: *And him that hath the grace of a good spirit he loveth as his own soul.* The Testament of Benjamin (DB ch 89 v.5) names the love-thy-brother-as-thine-own-soul measure in the patriarch's good-mind teaching — the good man *loveth the righteous as his own soul,* shielding, showing mercy, overcoming evil with good. John 15:13's *Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends* lands the same architecture at its furthest reach: the love-as-thine-own-soul of the fathers' testimony brought to the laying-down of the soul itself. The Hebrew library named the measure; the gospel walks it to the cross.
new_note: *Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.* (John 15:13). *And him that hath the grace of a good spirit he loveth as his own soul.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 134:5). Yahusha (Jesus) names the greatest love as laying down one's life for his friends. Benjamin teaches his sons the same love at its starting measure: the man with the grace of a good spirit loves his brother as his own soul. A man who loves another as his own soul has already begun to hold his own life loosely, and the Messiah (Christ) carries that love to its furthest end.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 134:5 — *him that hath the grace of a good spirit he loveth as his own soul.* Benjamin teaches loving a brother as one's own soul, the measure that John 15:13 carries to laying down one's life.
drafter_flag: Old note cited 'DB ch 89 v.5' (stale) and its italic quote ('loveth the righteous as his own soul') is not what the live verse says; I quote the live 134:5.

old_note: *And such was the appearance of their countenances, of a lion, of a man, of an ox, of an eagle: four heads were upon their bodies, so that the four creatures had sixteen faces; and each had six wings from their shoulders, and their sides, and their loins.* (Apocalypse of Abraham 18:4). The Hebrew library names the four faces and the six wings together — *of a lion, of a man, of an ox, of an eagle... and each had six wings.* John beholds exactly this: the four faces *like a lion... like a calf... a face as a man... like a flying eagle* (Revelation 4:7), and *the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within* (Revelation 4:8). The same lion-man-ox-eagle, the same six wings; one throne-vision held across the restored library.
new_note: *And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Yahuah Elohim (Lord God) Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come.* (Revelation 4:8). *And such was the appearance of their countenances, of a lion, of a man, of an ox, of an eagle: four heads were upon their bodies, so that the four creatures had sixteen faces; and each had six wings from their shoulders, and their sides, and their loins.* (Apocalypse of Abraham 18:4). John sees four beasts with six wings each, full of eyes, who rest not day and night as they say Holy, holy, holy. The verse before gives their four faces: *And the first beast was like a lion, and the second beast like a calf, and the third beast had a face as a man, and the fourth beast was like a flying eagle.* (Revelation 4:7). Abraham is shown the same creatures under the throne: a lion, a man, an ox and an eagle, with six wings each. Two witnesses see the same four faces and the same six wings around the throne.
member_note: Apocalypse of Abraham 18:4 — *of a lion, of a man, of an ox, of an eagle: four heads were upon their bodies.* Abraham's four faced creatures with six wings are the beasts around the throne in Revelation 4:8.

old_note: Isaiah 14:12 — *How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!* The prophet's son-of-the-morning is the very bright one whom Elohim says He deprived of his bright nature so that he became dark.
new_note: *But when he transgressed My commandment, I deprived him of that bright nature, and he became dark.* (1 Adam and Eve 13:3). *How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!* (Isaiah 14:12). Isaiah speaks of one who fell from heaven, called the son of the morning, and cut down to the ground. In 1 Adam and Eve, Elohim (God) tells Adam of an angel who once carried a bright light and lost it by breaking the commandment, so that he became dark. The two verses describe the same fall from two sides: Isaiah names the height and the cutting down, and Elohim (God) names what was taken from him. Both say that the one who fell had been bright before he transgressed.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 13:3 — *I deprived him of that bright nature, and he became dark.* Isaiah's son of the morning is the bright one who lost his light when he broke the commandment.

new_note: *And Adam began to make more requests of Elohim (God). * ORIGINAL OF THE LORD'S PRAYER SAID TO BE USED ABOUT 150 YEARS BEFORE OUR Yahuah (God): Our Father, Who art in Heaven, be gracious unto us, O Yahuah (Lord) our Elohim (God), hallowed be Your Name, and let the remembrance of Thee be glorified Heaven above and upon earth here below. Let Your kingdom reign over us now and forever. The Holy Men of old said remit and forgive unto all men whatsoever they have done unto me. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil thing; for Thine is the kingdom and Thou shalt reign in glory forever and forevermore, AMEN.* (1 Adam and Eve 23:9). *And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.* (Matthew 6:13). Adam keeps asking Elohim (God) for more, and the prayer put in his mouth ends on the same petitions Yahusha (Jesus) gives his disciples: do not lead us into temptation, deliver us from the evil, for the kingdom is Yours. The wording is not identical, since Adam's version says the evil thing and has a longer opening, but the shape is the same: a plea for rescue and a confession that the kingdom belongs to Yahuah (the Lord) alone. The first man prays it after the fall, and Matthew records the same cry for those who follow him now.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 23:9 — *lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil thing; for Thine is the kingdom.* Adam's prayer asks for deliverance and confesses the kingdom as Elohim's, as Matthew 6:13 does.

old_note: Hebrews 9:22 — *And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.* That Adam could only sue for forgiveness through blood in 1-adam-eve 24:5 is the law Hebrews states — no remission without shed blood, the necessity that drives the whole apparatus to the cross.
new_note: *And as you sued for forgiveness through that blood, so also will I make My blood forgiveness of sins, and erase transgressions in it.* (1 Adam and Eve 24:5). *And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.* (Hebrews 9:22). Adam has shed his blood on an altar and sought forgiveness through it, and the Word of Elohim (God) answers that He will make His own blood the forgiveness of sins. Hebrews states the same necessity plainly: under the law almost everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no remission. The law is not set aside here; it is the very ground the promise to Adam stands on, and the one who comes in the flesh of Adam's descendants, Yahusha (Jesus), answers it with His own blood.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 24:5 — *so also will I make My blood forgiveness of sins, and erase transgressions in it.* What Adam sought through blood, the Word promises to supply with His own, as Hebrews 9:22 says no remission comes without it.

old_note: Hebrews 6:15 — *And so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise.* Adam's calling-of-the-soul to bear long until the covenant (1 Adam & Eve 26:11) is the patient endurance by which the fathers obtained the promise.
new_note: *Yes, rather, bear long and calm your soul while you live night and day; until the fulfillment of the days, and the time of My covenant is come.* (1 Adam and Eve 26:11). *And so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise.* (Hebrews 6:15). Elohim (God) tells Adam to bear long and calm his soul until the days of the covenant are fulfilled, and the next verse says He will come and save him. Hebrews says Abraham obtained the promise in just this way, by patiently enduring. The promise does not come by hurry; it comes at the time Elohim (God) has set, to the one who waits for it. Adam is told to wait, and Abraham is shown having done it.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 26:11 — *bear long and calm your soul while you live night and day; until the fulfillment of the days.* Adam is told to wait out the days until the covenant, and Abraham obtained the promise by patient endurance.

old_note: Jubilees 3:5 — *And Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) caused a deep sleep to fall upon him, and he slept, and He took for the woman one rib from amongst his ribs, and this rib was the origin of the woman from amongst his ribs, and He built up the flesh in its stead, and built the woman.* The restored Jubilees keeps the same rib-drawn-in-sleep that Adam rehearses in 34:14.
new_note: *Then You drew a rib out of my side, and created it after my own likeness and image. Then I awoke; and when I saw her and knew who she was, I said, 'This is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; from now on she shall be called woman.'* (1 Adam and Eve 34:14). *And Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) caused a deep sleep to fall upon him, and he slept, and He took for the woman one rib from amongst his ribs, and this rib was the origin of the woman from amongst his ribs, and He built up the flesh in its stead, and built the woman.* (Jubilees 3:5). Adam recalls that he slept, that a rib was drawn from his side, and that he woke to see the woman and name her. Jubilees tells the same event from the other side: Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) caused the deep sleep, took one rib, and built the woman from it. The two accounts agree on the sleep and the rib, and each says what the other leaves out: Adam speaks as the one who slept and woke, and Jubilees speaks of the hand that built her.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 34:14 — *Then You drew a rib out of my side, and created it after my own likeness and image.* Adam tells of the rib and the sleep from his own side, and Jubilees 3:5 tells the same from Yahuah's.

old_note: Romans 5:12 — *Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:* Adam's wonder that he was not struck dead at once (34:11) is the same death-by-one-man Sha'ul traces from this transgression.
new_note: *And if You had punished me as You said, with death, I should have died that very moment.* (1 Adam and Eve 34:11). *Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:* (Romans 5:12). Adam looks back on the day he ate and marvels that he was not struck dead on the spot, as the command had said he would be. Paul traces the same line: by one man sin entered into the world, and death came through sin. What Adam says of himself in his own telling, the apostle says of him for all who came after, that the death spoken over the tree reached everyone through the one who ate.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 34:11 — *if You had punished me as You said, with death, I should have died that very moment.* Adam's wonder that death did not strike at once is the death by one man that Paul traces in Romans 5:12.

old_note: Jubilees 4:30 — *And he lacked seventy years of one thousand years; for one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens and therefore was it written concerning the tree of knowledge: “On the day that you eat thereof you will die.” For this reason he did not complete the years of this day; for he died during it.* The same day-as-a-thousand-years testimony of the heavens stands behind the 5500-year promise of 1-adam-eve 38:2.
new_note: *"O Adam, as to the fruit on the Tree of Life that you have asked for, I will not give it to you now, but only when the 5500 years are fulfilled. At that time I will give you fruit from the Tree of Life, and you will eat, and live forever, you, and Eve, and your righteous descendants.* (1 Adam and Eve 38:2). *And he lacked seventy years of one thousand years; for one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens and therefore was it written concerning the tree of knowledge: “On the day that you eat thereof you will die.” For this reason he did not complete the years of this day; for he died during it.* (Jubilees 4:30). Elohim (God) tells Adam that the fruit of the Tree of Life is held back until the 5500 years are fulfilled, and then he and Eve and their righteous descendants will eat and live forever. Jubilees shows how the heavens count such spans: a thousand years are as one day, and Adam, lacking seventy years of a thousand, died within the day of the command about the tree. The long wait Adam is given is counted in these days of the heavens.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 38:2 — *I will not give it to you now, but only when the 5500 years are fulfilled.* The wait given to Adam is counted in the days of a thousand years that Jubilees 4:30 describes.

old_note: 2 Peter 3:8 — *But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with Yahuah (Lord) as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.* The 5500-year count of 1-adam-eve 38:2 is reckoned by this day-for-a-thousand-years measure pointing to the Saviour's day.
new_note: *"O Adam, as to the fruit on the Tree of Life that you have asked for, I will not give it to you now, but only when the 5500 years are fulfilled. At that time I will give you fruit from the Tree of Life, and you will eat, and live forever, you, and Eve, and your righteous descendants.* (1 Adam and Eve 38:2). *But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with Yahuah (Lord) as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.* (2 Peter 3:8). Elohim (God) promises Adam the fruit of the Tree of Life only when the 5500 years are fulfilled, a span counted in thousands. Peter tells his beloved not to be ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with Yahuah (the Lord) as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. That is the scale on which Elohim (God) speaks when He tells Adam to wait: what looks to Adam like a very long delay is a few days to the one who made him, and the promise is held to its appointed day.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 38:2 — *only when the 5500 years are fulfilled.* The span set before Adam is measured on the scale Peter names, a day with Yahuah being a thousand years.

old_note: Revelation 22:14 — *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.* The eating-and-living-forever pledged to Adam's righteous descendants in 1-adam-eve 38:2 belongs to those who keep the commandments.
new_note: *"O Adam, as to the fruit on the Tree of Life that you have asked for, I will not give it to you now, but only when the 5500 years are fulfilled. Elohim (God) promises Adam, Eve and their righteous descendants that they will eat of the Tree of Life and live forever when the time is fulfilled. The last chapter of Revelation says who has the right to that tree: those who do His commandments, who then enter the city through its gates. The righteous descendants of Adam are the ones who keep the commandments, so the promise at the beginning and the blessing at the end are one promise, and the commandments are the way to it.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 38:2 — *you will eat, and live forever, you, and Eve, and your righteous descendants.* The tree promised to Adam's righteous descendants is the tree open to those who do His commandments in Revelation 22:14.

The water promised to Adam's line in the first days is the same water offered to the one who believes in Yahusha (Jesus), and it comes through His blood.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 42:8 — *My blood shall be the Water of Life to you at that time.* The Water of Life promised to Adam's believing descendants is the rivers of living water Yahusha gives in John 7:38.

old_note: Genesis 4:26 — *And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* Adam's praying for forgiveness in 1 Adam and Eve 47:6 is the first keeping of this same calling-on-the-Name that runs down the holy seed-line.
new_note: *And they stood and prayed Elohim (God) to forgive them their sins, and then fell asleep under the summit of the mountain.* (1 Adam and Eve 47:6). *And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* (Genesis 4:26). Adam and Eve stand and pray to Elohim (God) to forgive them, and then sleep under the mountain. Genesis marks the line of Seth, and the days of his son Enos, as the time when men began to call upon the name of Yahuah (the LORD). The prayer of Adam and Eve is the same calling, already on their lips: forgiveness sought from Elohim (God) by name, and carried down by the holy seed.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 47:6 — *they stood and prayed Elohim (God) to forgive them their sins.* Adam and Eve's prayer for forgiveness is the same calling on the Name that Genesis 4:26 records in Enos's day.
drafter_flag: Genesis 4:26 dates the beginning of calling on the Name to Enos, so I tied the two as the same practice carried down the seed-line and did not call Adam's prayer the first keeping of it, which the old note had said.

old_note: 1 Corinthians 15:4 — *And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:* The buried-and-third-day-risen gospel Paul calls first of all is the very word spoken to Adam under the rock, rising on the third day according to the scriptures written from the beginning.

Paul gives the gospel in the same order: He was buried, and He rose again the third day according to the scriptures. Adam heard it first, under the rock, long before it happened, and Paul's phrase according to the scriptures reaches back to that beginning.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 49:9 — *on the third day I shall rise again, and it shall be salvation to you, O Adam.* The third day rising spoken to Adam is the gospel Paul gives in 1 Corinthians 15:4.

Moses was with Yahuah (the LORD) forty days and forty nights in the same way, neither eating bread nor drinking water, and wrote the words of the covenant. Both men stand empty in the presence of Elohim (God) for forty days, one seeking forgiveness and the other receiving the covenant.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 71:6 — *He neither ate nor drank until he dropped down on the ground from hunger and thirst.* Adam's forty days without food or drink in prayer matches Moses' forty days before Yahuah in Exodus 34:28.

old_note: Genesis 4:26 — *And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* Adam's offering for his newborns at 1-adam-eve 74:9 belongs to the same calling-on-the-Name that marks the covenant line from the first.
new_note: *Then Adam and Eve waited until Cain and his sister were forty days old, when Adam said to Eve, "We will make an offering and offer it up in behalf of the children."* (1 Adam and Eve 74:9). *And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* (Genesis 4:26). Adam and Eve wait until their children are forty days old and then say they will make an offering on the children's behalf. Genesis records that in the days of Enos men began to call upon the name of Yahuah (the LORD). Offering for the newborn is part of that calling: the first family brings its children before Elohim (God) at the start of their lives, and Genesis names the line in which the practice becomes known.
member_note: 1 Adam and Eve 74:9 — *We will make an offering and offer it up in behalf of the children.* Adam and Eve's offering for their children belongs to the calling on Yahuah's name that Genesis 4:26 records.

old_note: John 8:44 — *Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. new_note: *THEN Elohim (God) ordered Satan to show himself to Adam plainly, in his own hideous form.* (2 Adam and Eve 4:1). *Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.* (John 8:44). Yahusha (Jesus) names the same enemy in the same way: a murderer from the beginning, with no truth in him, a liar and the father of lying. Adam is shown the face of the liar, and Yahusha (Jesus) names what the liar does. Both put the lie and the killing at the root.
member_note: 2 Adam and Eve 4:1 — *Elohim (God) ordered Satan to show himself to Adam plainly, in his own hideous form.* Satan shown to Adam in his own form is the murderer and liar from the beginning whom Yahusha names in John 8:44.

old_note: Genesis 4:26 — *And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* The righteousness Enos commands Cainan to establish in 2 Adam and Eve 14:3 is the calling-on-the-Name that began in Enos’s own generation.
new_note: *Then Enos called his son Cainan and said to him, "See, 0 my son, and set thy heart on thy people, and establish them in righteousness, and in innocence; and stand ministering before the body of our father Adam, all the days of thy life."* (2 Adam and Eve 14:3). *And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* (Genesis 4:26). Enos charges his son Cainan to set his heart on his people, to establish them in righteousness and innocence, and to stand ministering before the body of Adam all his days. Genesis says that in the days of Enos, son of Seth, men began to call upon the name of Yahuah (the LORD). The charge to Cainan shows what that calling looked like in Enos's house: a righteous people kept in order, serving and making offerings in honor of their father Adam.
member_note: 2 Adam and Eve 14:3 — *stand ministering before the body of our father Adam, all the days of thy life.* Enos's charge to Cainan to keep a righteous people is the calling on the Name that Genesis 4:26 places in Enos's days.

old_note: Psalm 104:4 — *Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire.* Abraham's angels of pure spirit without bodies, serving the fiery angels, are the very spirits-and-flaming-ministers of the Psalm (Apocalypse of Abraham 19:6).
new_note: *And I looked from the mountain in which I stood downwards to the sixth firmament, and saw there a multitude of angels, of pure spirit, without bodies, who carried out the commands of the fiery angels who were upon the eighth firmament, as I was standing suspended over them.* (Apocalypse of Abraham 19:6). *Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire:* (Psalm 104:4). The psalm says that He makes His angels spirits and His ministers a flaming fire. The two lines match in order: the spirits who do the work below, and the fiery ones who command them from above. Abraham sees what the psalm says.
member_note: Apocalypse of Abraham 19:6 — *angels, of pure spirit, without bodies, who carried out the commands of the fiery angels.* The bodiless spirits serving fiery angels are the spirits and flaming ministers of Psalm 104:4.

old_note: Exodus 3:2 — *And the angel of Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.* The voice that speaks to Abraham from the midst of the fire is the same fire-that-does-not-consume that called Moses at Horeb (Apocalypse of Abraham 19:1).
new_note: *And a voice came to me out of the midst of the fire, saying: "Abraham, Abraham!"* (Apocalypse of Abraham 19:1). *And the angel of Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.* (Exodus 3:2). In both, the fire is the place from which the call comes, not a danger to the one being called. Yahuah (the LORD) meets the man He is calling in the fire.
member_note: Apocalypse of Abraham 19:1 — *a voice came to me out of the midst of the fire, saying.* The voice calling Abraham out of the fire is the fire from which Moses was called at the bush in Exodus 3:2.

old_note: Jude 1:14 — *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, Yahuah (Lord) cometh with ten thousands of his saints,* Jude's citation of Enoch sits beside the Lord coming with the armies of the holy ones in Ascension of Isaiah 4:14. The saints who come with him are the seed of promise, gathered and coming with him into the land — *and all the saints with thee* (Zechariah 14:5) — not angels, and not souls come down from heaven.
new_note: Jude 1:14 — *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, Yahuah (Lord) cometh with ten thousands of his saints,* Jude's word from Enoch sits beside the Ascension of Isaiah, where Yahuah (the Lord) comes with his angels and with the armies of the holy ones from the seventh heaven. The ten thousands of his saints are that company of holy ones who come with him — *and all the saints with thee* (Zechariah 14:5) — the coming Enoch foresaw and Isaiah was shown.
drafter_flag: FOR YOSHI: the old prose said the saints who come with him are the seed of promise 'not angels, and not souls come down from heaven'; the live Ascension of Isaiah 4:14 says he comes 'with His angels and with the armies of the holy ones from the seventh heaven'. Rewritten to what the two verses say together, without ruling on who the holy ones are. If the seed-of-promise reading is to stand here it needs its own witness quoted.

old_note: Isaiah 53:2 — *For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him.* The descent 'hidden even from the heavens' lands as Isaiah's own no-form-nor-comeliness — the prophet himself foretold the disguised coming.
new_note: *And thus His descent, as you will see, will be hidden even from the heavens, so that it will not be known who He is.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:15). *For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him.* (Isaiah 53:2). The Ascension of Isaiah says the Son's coming down will be hidden even from the heavens, so that none will know who He is. The powers of heaven did not recognize him as he passed through, and the people on earth did not see anything in him to desire.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 9:15 — *His descent, as you will see, will be hidden even from the heavens.* The descent hidden from the heavens matches Isaiah's tender plant with no form or comeliness.

old_note: Revelation 5:12 — *Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.* The praise that increased in volume through the heavens is the heavenly worthy-is-the-Lamb of John's throne-room.
new_note: *Both worshipped Him and praised Him and said: "How did our Lord escape us whilst descending, and we perceived not?"* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:26). *Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.* (Revelation 5:12). In the Ascension of Isaiah, the powers of the heavens worship the Beloved as he passes through and ask how He went by them unseen, and at each heaven the same praise is given again. John's vision of the throne room has the same voice going up, loud and many: Worthy is the Lamb that was slain. The praise the angels give in Isaiah's vision is the praise of Revelation, given to the one who was slain.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:26 — *How did our Lord escape us whilst descending, and we perceived not?.* The heavens worship the Beloved who passed through unseen, as they cry Worthy is the Lamb in Revelation.

old_note: John 6:35 — *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.* The descending manna of the Messiah's years finds its substance in the Anointed Himself, the bread of life on whom the saved feed and never hunger.
new_note: *And it shall come to pass at that self-same time that the treasury of manna shall again descend from on high, and they will eat of it in those years, because these are they who have come to the consummation of time.* (2 Baruch 29:8). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.* (John 6:35). In the years of the Messiah, 2 Baruch says, the treasury of manna will again descend from on high, and they will eat of it. The bread that came down for the tribes in the wilderness is promised again for the end of time. Yahusha (Jesus) says of himself that he is the bread of life, and that the one who comes to him shall never hunger and the one who believes on him shall never thirst. The bread from on high that Baruch looks for is the one standing before them in John.
member_note: 2 Baruch 29:8 — *the treasury of manna shall again descend from on high.* The manna promised again from on high is the bread of life Yahusha (Jesus) names himself.
drafter_flag: Old note's phrase 'the saved feed' removed. Kept the connection; nothing added.

old_note: Rev 21:4 — *there shall be no more death... for the former things are passed away* — the corruptible consummated and the incorruptible begun, Baruch's near-to-things-which-die-not.
new_note: *For that time is the consummation of that which is corruptible, And the beginning of that which is not corruptible. Therefore those things which were predicted shall belong to it: Therefore it is far away from evils, and near to those things which die not.* (2 Baruch 74:2–3) *And Elohim (God) shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.* (Revelation 21:4) John sees the same turning in Revelation. When the corruptible reaches its end the incorruptible begins, and Baruch says that age is far from evils and near to those things which die not, which is what John means when there is no more death. Elohim (God) wipes the tears away because the former things have passed, and both writers are looking at the same line between this age and the one that does not end.
member_note: 2 Baruch 74:2 — *the consummation of that which is corruptible, And the beginning of that which is not corruptible.* John sees the same passing in Revelation 21:4, where there is no more death because the former things are passed away.
drafter_flag: Old note leaned on 'near to those things which die not' (2 Baruch 74:3), so I quoted 74:2 and 74:3 together and cited 74:2–3; no move needed.

old_note: Psalm 110:4 — *Yahuah (LORD) hath sworn, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek).* The new priest 'to whom there shall none succeed for ever' is the priest sworn for ever after Melchizedek.
new_note: Psalm 110:4 — *Yahuah (LORD) hath sworn, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek).* The new priest Yahuah (the Lord) raises up, to whom all his words are revealed and who judges the earth for a multitude of days, is the priest Yahuah (the LORD) swore in after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek) — a priesthood not from Levi's line and not for a season.
drafter_flag: The old prose quoted 'to whom there shall none succeed for ever', words not in the live Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 34:2; rewritten to what 34:2 says (a new priest raised up, all the words of Yahuah revealed to him, judging for a multitude of days).

old_note: John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* — "God shall appear, dwelling among men on earth" is fulfilled when the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us — the Father made manifest in the Son He sent.
new_note: John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* — "God shall appear, dwelling among men on earth" is fulfilled when the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us — the only begotten whom the Father sent, the Formed one walking among men.

old_note: 1 Pet 3:18 — *For Messiah (Christ) also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to Elohim (God).* — the just-for-the-unjust the testament foresees, "a sinless shall die for ungodly men."
new_note: *In thee shall be fulfilled the prophecy of heaven [concerning the Lamb of Elohim (God), and Saviour of the world], that a blameless one shall be delivered up for lawless men, and a sinless shall die for ungodly men [in the blood of the covenant, for the salvation of the Gentiles and 'of Israel', and shall destroy Beliar and his servants].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:8). *For Messiah (Christ) also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to Elohim (God), being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit:* (1 Peter 3:18). Jacob, embracing Joseph, says that in him the prophecy of heaven will be fulfilled: a blameless one delivered up for lawless men and a sinless one dying for ungodly men. Peter says it of the Messiah (Christ), who suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, so that He might bring us to Elohim (God). The two lines carry the same shape, the righteous one giving himself for those who are not, and the end of it is bringing the lost home to the Father.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:8 — *a blameless one shall be delivered up for lawless men, and a sinless shall die for ungodly men.* Jacob foretells a sinless one dying for ungodly men, and Peter names the Messiah (Christ) as the just one who suffered for the unjust.

old_note: Matt 5:44 — *Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.* — the praying-for-them-that-wrong-you that Joseph embodied before his brethren.
new_note: *For Joseph also besought our father 'that he would pray for his brethren', that 'the Lord' would not impute to them as sin whatever evil they had done unto him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:6). *But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;* (Matthew 5:44). His brothers had done Joseph evil, and Joseph asked their father to pray for them and that Yahuah (the Lord) would not count it to them as sin. That is Matthew 5:44 lived before it was spoken: praying for those who despitefully use you and persecute you. Benjamin hands the story to his sons as proof that loving an enemy can be done, even when the enemy is your own brother.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:6 — *besought our father 'that he would pray for his brethren', that 'the Lord' would not impute to them as sin.* Joseph asked his father to pray for the brothers who wronged him, which is the love of enemies Yahusha (Jesus) later commands.
